basis: Microcephaly and chorioretinal disease define this inherited neurodevelopmental syndrome; inflammatory ancestry alone does not establish immune causation.
Secondary pigmentary degeneration of the retina.
Occlusion of a retinal arterial branch directly affects the retinal circulation and eye.
Congenital absence of skin; no additional organ involvement established for this inheritance-defined concept.
Umbrella disorder of the brain, spinal cord or peripheral nerves; additional axes are subtype-specific.
Leucine catabolic defect; most identified patients are asymptomatic. Severe neurologic findings in tiny HPO series do not establish involvement in >=30% overall.
Renal acidification defect with acidosis and hypokalemia; sensorineural hearing loss in 9/23 (~39%). Rickets in 2/9 (~22%) falls below threshold.
Usher type 1G is defined by sensorineural deafness, vestibular dysfunction and progressive rod-cone retinal dystrophy.
Multiple benign subcutaneous lipomas; thrombocytopenia is very rare (1-4%).
Deficiency of lectin-pathway complement activation is an immunodeficiency; no common direct organ damage is established across the group.
Hypoplastic gonads cause hypogonadism and failure of secondary sexual development, establishing endocrine dysfunction.
Brenner tumor of the vagina affects a reproductive organ outside the 13 axes.
Tumor of the sphenoid paranasal sinus, included in the airway axis; skull involvement and lymphoma mechanism are not universal.
Cyst of fallopian-tube or broad-ligament origin; purely reproductive anatomy without defined endocrine dysfunction.
Intellectual impairment is a defining neurodevelopmental loss of function; associated organ abnormalities depend on the underlying subtype.
Cancer originating in the fallopian-tube isthmus; reproductive anatomy has no axis.
Bartonella infection produces characteristic cutaneous vascular proliferative lesions; visceral involvement is variable and not established in >=30%.
Cerebral hemispheric overgrowth and cortical malformation cause epilepsy and developmental impairment. Cranial asymmetry alone does not establish skeletal damage.
Neoplasm affecting the adrenal cortex, an endocrine gland; functional hormone secretion is not required for this axis.
Benign vascular neoplasm arising within the brain or meninges, defining both intracranial and blood-vessel involvement.
Respiratory-chain metabolic defect; encephalopathy and skeletal myopathy each occur commonly (~30%+) across major forms. Cardiac and renal damage vary by subtype.
Brugada syndrome is a cardiac electrical disorder with ventricular arrhythmia risk; SCN1B alone does not establish neurologic involvement.
Xerotic dermatitis of eyelid skin; eyelids are explicitly included in the ocular axis.
Malignant neoplasm affecting the lacrimal drainage system, which belongs to the ocular axis.
Sensorineural hearing loss defines the ear involvement. Infertility reflects defective sperm structure and motility, without established endocrine dysfunction.
